result.rationale: The handler's dedupe filter `!booking.attendees.some((attendee) => guest === attendee.email)` uses exact case-sensitive comparison, and zod's `z.string().email()` in addGuests.schema.ts does not normalize case. So a case-variant of an existing attendee email bypasses uniqueness and is persisted via createMany, duplicating the attendee (double emails, double ICS listing). The diff also shows case-normalization elsewhere only for the blacklist (`.toLowerCase()`), confirming the guest-vs-attendee comparison is left unnormalized. This breaks the endpoint's uniqueness invariant.

judged_text: The dedupe filter compares guest emails to stored attendee emails with case-sensitive === (line 76), and neither zod's .email() nor the filter normalizes case, so a case-variant of an already-added attendee ('Guest@Example.com' vs stored 'guest@example.com') passes as unique. createMany persists a second Attendee row for the same person, who then appears twice in the booking's attendee list, receives two separate emails, and is listed twice in the calendar event ICS — the uniqueness invariant this endpoint exists to enforce is broken by ordinary mixed-case typing.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the dedupe logic uses strict, case-sensitive equality (`guest === attendee.email`) when filtering out already-existing attendees, and neither the Zod schema (`z.string().email()`) nor the handler normalizes emails (e.g., `toLowerCase()`). As a result, a case-variant of an existing attendee email (e.g., `Guest@Example.com` vs stored `guest@example.com`) will be treated as unique and inserted via `attendees.createMany`, leading to duplicate attendee rows and downstream duplication in attendee lists/emails/calendar updates.
